english.title: Open door / leave a train whilst still in motion / between stations on the Tyne and Wear Metro
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) whilst upon the Tyne and Wear Metro

(A)_[opened a door or attempted to open a door of]_
(B)_[entered or attempted to enter]_
(C)_[left or attempted to leave]_

a train whilst it was

(D)_[in motion]_
(E)_[between stations]_
english.legislation: Contrary to byelaws 10(3) and 31(1) of the Tyne and Wear Metro Byelaws made under sections 58 and 62 of the Tyneside Metropolitan Railway Act 1973.

english.notes:
(i) Byelaw 30 make provisions in relation to name and addresses.
(ii) Byelaw 31(2) provides powers for the removal of persons.
(iii) When using these powers, an authorised person, including a constable, must show his/her identification if requested.
(iv) There are other byelaws which may be more appropriate depending on the circumstances, as well as other normal public order, indecency, damage, harassment and litter offences which may be worth considering.
(v) Byelaw 31(6) provides that in relation to this byelaw: An authorised person acting in the course of his duties shall not be liable for breach of this byelaw.
(vi) Byelaw 31(4) provides that no person shall be subject to any penalty for breach of any of the Byelaws by disobeying a notice unless it is proved to the satisfaction of the Court before whom the complaint is laid that the notice referred to in the particular Byelaw was displayed.
(vii) Byelaw 31(5) provides that any person who attempts to breach this byelaw shall be liable to the same penalty as for the full offence.
